# Story RT-3: `/retrofit-team` slash command (orchestrator overlay)

## Status: complete

## User Story

As a bmad-swarm user with an existing project that has an architecture but no Domain Map,
I want a `/retrofit-team` slash command that proposes a Domain Map for me, lets me iterate, asks for explicit approval, and inserts it into `architecture.md`,
So that I do not have to manually author the section while still keeping full editorial control over what lands in the file.

## Acceptance Criteria

### AC1: `/retrofit-team` slash command file is generated by `commands-generator.js`

**Given** the project after this story lands and after `bmad-swarm update` runs
**Then** `.claude/commands/retrofit-team.md` exists
**And** the file's body matches the specification in §3.2 of `architecture-retrofit.md`
**And** the file has the standard `---\ndescription: ...\n---` frontmatter

### AC2: Generator emits the new command in the WORKFLOWS array

**Given** the source of `generators/commands-generator.js`
**Then** the `WORKFLOWS` array contains an entry `{ name: 'retrofit-team', description: '...', body: buildRetrofitTeamBody() }`
**And** `buildRetrofitTeamBody()` returns a string containing the orchestrator instructions per `architecture-retrofit.md` §3.2

### AC3: Slash command body refuses when wide-team is already configured

**Given** the body's instruction set
**Then** step 1 explicitly tells the orchestrator to refuse if `swarm.yaml:team.mode === 'fixed'` AND `team.specializations` is non-empty
**And** the refuse message names the existing config and exits the overlay cleanly

### AC4: Slash command body refuses when `architecture.md` is missing

**Given** the body's instruction set
**Then** step 2 tells the orchestrator to refuse if `artifacts/design/architecture.md` does not exist
**And** the refuse message points the user at `/feature` or `/plan`

### AC5: Slash command body handles existing Domain Map

**Given** the body's instruction set
**Then** step 3 tells the orchestrator to detect an existing `## Domain Map` section
**And** if present, show it to the user and ask whether to refuse (default), append-as-comment, or replace
**And** the `replace` option requires the user to type the literal word `replace`

### AC6: Slash command body loads architect Domain Map heuristics

**Given** the body's instruction set
**Then** step 4 tells the orchestrator to read `agents/architect.md` (specifically the "Domain Map" section) and apply its four heuristics

### AC7: Slash command body waits for explicit human approval

**Given** the body's instruction set
**Then** step 7 says the orchestrator MUST pause and ask "approve the Domain Map for insertion into architecture.md?" before proceeding
**And** the body explicitly notes that this honors the CLAUDE.md `architecture` human-approval invariant

### AC8: Slash command body emits a single-task `bmad-assembly` block on approval

**Given** the body's instruction set
**Then** step 8 tells the orchestrator to emit a `bmad-assembly` block spawning ONE architect teammate
**And** the spawn brief explicitly includes the literal phrases "do not author a fresh Domain Map" and "do not write an ADR"
**And** the brief includes the Domain Map verbatim and the chosen insertion position

### AC9: Slash command body logs a tactical D-ID after the architect reports done

**Given** the body's instruction set
**Then** step 9 instructs the orchestrator to log to `decision-log.md` as a tactical entry: `D-NNN — Retrofit Domain Map added to architecture.md via /retrofit-team`

### AC10: Slash command body tells the user the next step

**Given** the body's instruction set
**Then** step 10 instructs the orchestrator to tell the user about `bmad-swarm scaffold-team` (RT-2) as the next action

### AC11: Generator unit test covers the new command

**Given** the existing pattern in `commands-generator.js` tests (if any) or new tests added
**Then** there is at least one assertion that the WORKFLOWS array includes the `retrofit-team` entry
**And** at least one snapshot or content-substring test for `buildRetrofitTeamBody()`'s output

### AC12: Existing slash commands are unaffected

**Given** the project after this story lands
**Then** every existing slash command (`/bug`, `/feature`, `/research`, `/audit`, `/brainstorm`, `/explore-idea`, `/migrate`, `/review`, `/plan`) is generated identically to before this story
**And** `commandResult.modified.length === 0` (no manually-modified files would be skipped because we only added one entry)

## Dev Notes

### Architecture Context

This story implements `architecture-retrofit.md` §3 (Tool A — `/retrofit-team` design) and **ADR-010** (overlay-vs-spawn decision: hybrid — overlay for design, spawn for the file edit).

The slash command body is **prose instructions for the orchestrator LLM**, not Node code that does the work. The structural pattern matches existing overlay commands `/brainstorm` and `/explore-idea` (see `commands-generator.js:buildBrainstormBody` and `:buildExploreIdeaBody`). Read both before writing the new body.

### Technical Implementation

**Body shape** — follow the structure of `buildBrainstormBody`:

```javascript
function buildRetrofitTeamBody() {
  return `Enter retrofit-team mode (orchestrator-overlay pattern, hybrid: overlay for design + architect spawn for the file edit). Per ADR-010, this command...

[step-by-step instructions matching architecture-retrofit.md §3.2]

[footer cross-reference to architecture-retrofit.md and ADR-010]
`;
}
```

**Refuse conditions** — covered in steps 1, 2, and 3 of the body. Each refuse instruction tells the orchestrator to print a specific user-facing message and exit the overlay (no further work, no decision-log entry).

**The `bmad-assembly` block (step 8)** — must follow the orchestrator's own invariants from `agents/orchestrator.md`. Concretely:

```bmad-assembly
entry_point: small-feature
complexity: 5
autonomy: auto
team:
  - role: architect
    model: opus
rationale: Insert approved Domain Map verbatim into architecture.md (one Edit, no design work; spawn brief constrains scope).
```

The architect's spawn-prompt brief is composed by the orchestrator and includes the approved Domain Map text. The body should give the orchestrator a template for the brief — see `architecture-retrofit.md` §3.3 for the wording.

**Insertion position (step 6's tail)** — the body should tell the orchestrator to apply the priority order from `architecture-retrofit.md` §3.4: after `## Components` / `## Architecture` / `## System Overview` if present; else before any `team`/`domain`-related section; else append at the end.

### File Locations

- Modify: `generators/commands-generator.js` (add `buildRetrofitTeamBody`, add WORKFLOWS entry)

- Regenerated (not committed by hand — produced by `bmad-swarm update`): `.claude/commands/retrofit-team.md`

### Dependencies

Depends on **RT-1** (Domain Map parser). The slash command body's "detect existing Domain Map" step (3) tells the orchestrator to use `findDomainMap` (from `utils/domain-map.js`) — but the orchestrator does this via Read+grep at the conceptual level, not by invoking the JS function. The JS parser is for Tool B (RT-2). The dependency on RT-1 here is conceptual: the format the parser locks (ADR-012) is the format the orchestrator must produce in step 5 (and the format the existing-Domain-Map detection step looks for).

If RT-1 has not landed when RT-3 starts, RT-3 can proceed — the slash command body refers to the Domain Map format documented in `agents/architect.md`, which is independent of the parser.

### Testing Approach

The slash command body is prose for an LLM. Behavioral correctness is verified by manual end-to-end (Task 5), not automated tests. Automated tests (Task 4) cover the structural assertions:

- The WORKFLOWS array entry exists.
- The generated file exists with the expected frontmatter.
- The body contains key phrases that downstream depends on (the architect-spawn template, the human-approval pause, the refuse conditions).

Use `node:test`, follow the pattern in existing generator tests if any.

For the manual end-to-end (Task 5), document the test session in the Dev Agent Record. Include screenshots or transcript excerpts if helpful.

### Anti-Patterns

- Do NOT have the slash command body instruct the orchestrator to write to `architecture.md` directly. Per ADR-010 §"Alternatives considered" A, the orchestrator-write-gate is intentionally not loosened. Use the architect spawn for the file edit.
- Do NOT skip the human-approval pause. Per CLAUDE.md invariant ("Human approval is required for: ... architecture") and `architecture-retrofit.md` §3.2 step 7.
- Do NOT instruct the orchestrator to invoke `bmad-swarm scaffold-team` automatically as a final step. Per `architecture-retrofit.md` §12 trade-off 5, the chain is decoupled — user runs the CLI command themselves.
- Do NOT instruct the architect spawn to write an ADR. The design happened in the overlay; the spawn is a write delegate. Per ADR-010 §"Decision" and `architecture-retrofit.md` §3.2 step 8.
- Do NOT generate a default "yes" answer for the replace prompt. Per `architecture-retrofit.md` §3.6, `replace` requires typing the literal word.
- Do NOT introduce a parallel architect-spawn flow that bypasses the overlay (e.g., "if the user passes --quick, skip the conversation"). Per ADR-010, the overlay IS the conversation; if the user wants no conversation, they should hand-write the Domain Map and run `scaffold-team`.

- Footer cross-refs three load-bearing anchors: `architecture-retrofit.md §3`, ADR-010 (overlay-vs-spawn rationale), ADR-003 (orchestrator-write-gate — explicit non-loosening: "this overlay does NOT loosen the gate; the architect spawn does the file edit"), CLAUDE.md (`architecture` human-approval invariant).
- Body's pattern matches `buildBrainstormBody` and `buildExploreIdeaBody` (D-BRN-1 / D-BRN-4 precedents) — visual and stylistic consistency with existing overlay slash commands.
- **Two design checks** flagged for reviewer sanity-check, both confirmed approved:
  1. **Task 5 manual smoke test deferred to post-RT-4 user-acceptance phase.** The slash command body is prose for an LLM and has no Node-side behavioral surface that automated tests can exercise. Unit tests cover all structural invariants. Smoke test is a non-blocking follow-up logged in this Change Log.
  2. **RT-3 doesn't import `utils/domain-map.js`.** The dependency on RT-1 is conceptual (shared format spec via `agents/architect.md` §Domain Map + ADR-012), not code-level. Story Dev Notes line 153 explicitly anticipated this. The body operates at LLM-Read+grep level; only RT-2's CLI (JS code) needs the parser.

### Reviewer notes (carried forward)

- **D-015 → verified** (status flipped in decision-log).
- **Non-blocking follow-up:** Task 5 (manual end-to-end smoke test) deferred to post-RT-4 phase. After `bmad-swarm update` ships `.claude/commands/retrofit-team.md` to a real project, the user naturally exercises the slash command end-to-end. Verify the architect performs exactly one Edit, exits, and the decision-log entry lands per step 9. This is the same posture used by every other slash command in the repo — none have automated end-to-end smoke tests because the LLM-conversational layer doesn't admit them.
- The footer line "ADR-003 (orchestrator-write-gate — this overlay does NOT loosen the gate; the architect spawn does the file edit)" is doing two jobs: documenting the design choice AND serving as a tripwire for any future maintainer tempted to simplify the architecture by extending the orchestrator's write allow-list. Preserve this line on any future edit.
- Step 9's failure-mode clause ("If the architect spawn fails or rejects the brief, do NOT log the D-ID; report the failure to the user and exit") is correct posture — D-IDs only get logged when decisions are realized, not when intended.
- Subtle drift risk: RT-3 body and RT-1 parser are anchored to the same upstream spec but have no automated cross-check. Acceptable because any drift fails loudly at the moment of use (parser rejects orchestrator output OR accepts output the orchestrator didn't intend). Observed; not a finding.
